lessons.label: Lesson 4 — 20–99 compounds

notes: ja / lesson-4 — Japanese Numbers: 20-99 (compounds)
Applied VERBATIM from the Japanese linguistics dataset review. Fully regular:
[ten] + [ones], e.g. 21 = 二十一 ni-juu-ichi. Answer stacks kanji | romaji via
the engine's " | " separator. Learner-safe readings held across the whole
range: 4 = yon, 7 = nana, 9 = kyuu.

lessons.label: Lesson 5 — Big Number Roots
lessons.title: Japanese Big Number Roots
notes: ja / lesson-5 — Japanese Big Number Roots (roots × multipliers 1-9)
Applied VERBATIM from the Japanese linguistics dataset review.
6 root families (hundreds, thousands, millions, billions, trillions,
quadrillions) × 9 multipliers = 54, PLUS the 2 standalone myriad roots
MYRIAD grouping applied per the dataset: Japanese counts in powers of 10,000
(万 man = 10^4, 億 oku = 10^8, 兆 chou = 10^12). So 1,000,000 = 百万 hyaku-man
and 1,000,000,000 = 十億 juu-oku — NOT Western place-grouping. Irregulars kept
as delivered (memorized rendaku/gemination): 300 = san-byaku, 600 = roppyaku,
800 = happyaku, 3,000 = san-zen, 8,000 = hassen, 1T = icchou, 8T = hatchou,
and the million/quadrillion rows inherit the same changes. 10,000 MUST keep
its digit (一万 ichi-man), unlike bare sen (1,000). Answer stacks kanji | romaji
via the engine's " | " separator; prompts stay comma-formatted strings,
byte-identical to the reference deck.

lessons.label: Lesson 6 — Number Builder

notes: ja / lesson-6 — Japanese Number Builder
Applied VERBATIM from the Japanese linguistics dataset review. Keeps the
10-second reveal (revealMs: 10000). The answer stacks with the engine's " | "
separator: line 1 = full kanji, then ONE romaji line per MYRIAD group. Japanese
chunks by 万/億/兆, so the split lands on the myriad boundary (10,000) — this
differs from the thousand-based split other decks use, and that difference is
the point of teaching Japanese grouping. Hint = full pronunciation, one string.
